headline_marked: Kaptai Lake rises: [[Hanging bridge submerged]] in Rangamati
headline: Kaptai Lake rises: Hanging bridge submerged in Rangamati
summary: Heavy rains have caused water levels to rise in Kaptai Lake and the Kachalong river, leading to flooding in low-lying areas and the suspension of visitor entry to the bridge.
details: The hanging bridge on Kaptai Lake in Rangamati was submerged under four inches of water on Friday afternoon, following two days of continuous rainfall.
Authorities at the Rangamati Parjatan Holiday Complex have suspended visitor entry and ticket sales for the bridge, which will be reopened once water levels recede.
Rising water in the Kachalong river has also inundated low-lying areas of Baghaichhari upazila, including parts of the municipality and several unions.
The district weather observation centre recorded 67mm of rainfall in Rangamati over Thursday and Friday, with forecasts suggesting rain may continue for several more days.
To ease pressure on Kaptai Lake, authorities may open all 16 spillway gates of the Kaptai Dam at 10:00pm tonight.
An emergency notice from the Karnafuli Hydro Power Station stated the lake's water level reached 32.20m at 2:00pm, nearing its maximum capacity of 33.22 feet.

The district weather observation centre recorded 67mm of rainfall in Rangamati over Thursday and Friday, with forecasts suggesting rain may continue for several more days.

To ease pressure on Kaptai Lake, authorities may open all 16 spillway gates of the Kaptai Dam at 10:00pm tonight.

headline_marked: 996 hospitalised in 24 hours as [[2 more die of dengue]]
headline: 996 hospitalised in 24 hours as 2 more die of dengue
summary: The total number of hospitalisations this year has reached 33,586, with 90 deaths recorded so far, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
details: Two people died of dengue fever in the last 24 hours, while 996 new patients were admitted to hospitals across Bangladesh.
According to a notice from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) issued on Saturday, the new admissions were spread across various divisions.
Dhaka division saw the highest number of admissions with 391 patients, followed by Khulna with 263, and Barishal with 134.
Other affected areas include Chittagong (103), Mymensingh (45), Rajshahi (36), Rangpur (21), and Sylhet (3).
This brings the total number of dengue hospitalisations for the current year to 33,586.
The total death toll from dengue fever this year has now reached 90 people.
